title: Resolution-unit normalization of flat ringed derived exchange
statement:
Let four sites be small in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], each carrying a sheaf of commutative rings and its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Fix a commutative square of ringed-topos morphisms [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] with vertical edges $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$, $f':\mathcal X'\to\mathcal Y'$ and horizontal edges $g:\mathcal Y'\to\mathcal Y$, $g':\mathcal X'\to\mathcal X$, including its ring-compatible commutation isomorphism. Suppose the tensor pullbacks $g^*,(g')^*$ are exact. Use the module adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], ordinary derived categories with localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and canonical total right derived pairs $(Rf_*,\eta^f),(Rf'_*,\eta^{f'})$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Thus $\eta^f_P:Q(f_*P)\to Rf_*(QP)$ is the resolution transformation. Let $e:g^*f_*\to f'_*(g')^*$ be the underived adjunction mate of the square, and let $\beta:Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*L(g')^*$ be its canonical derived adjunction mate [def-trf-topos-derived-base-change-map]. For every bounded below module complex $P$ on $\mathcal X$, without injectivity or acyclicity hypotheses on its terms, the following equality holds under the exact termwise identifications $Lg^*Q=Qg^*$ and $L(g')^*Q=Q(g')^*$:
$$\beta_{QP}\circ g^*(\eta^f_P)=\eta^{f'}_{(g')^*P}\circ Q(e_P).$$
Here $e_P$ is termwise application of the underived mate. This asserts equality for the specified transformations and does not assert that $\beta$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0736 (lemma-base-change-map-flat-case), proof on injective resolutions, and remark-base-change (Tag 07A7), identification with the derived adjunction mate. Resolution-unit equality for arbitrary bounded below representatives is the naturality of this construction.

proof.text:
Write $A=g^*$, $B=(g')^*$, $a=g_*$, $b=(g')_*$, $R=f_*$ and $S=f'_*$. A bar denotes the specified total right derived functor, and $\eta^T:QT\to\bar TQ$ its resolution transformation. By exactness, the derived horizontal left adjoints are termwise $A,B$. Use the normalized ringed lifts for these adjunctions. Let $u:1\to bB$ and $c:Aa\to1$ be the ordinary horizontal unit and counit, and $u^D:1\to\bar bB$, $c^D:A\bar a\to1$ their derived versions. The canonical Hom normalization, applied to $1_{BP}$ and to $c_T:AaT\to T$, gives, for every complex $P$ on $\mathcal X$ and $T$ on $\mathcal Y'$,
$$u^D_{QP}=\eta^b_{BP}\,Q(u_P),\qquad c^D_{QT}\,A(\eta^a_T)=Q(c_T).$$
Indeed the ordinary transposes of these two chain maps are respectively $u_P$ and $1_{aT}$; the latter equality says that the inverse derived transpose of $\eta^a_T$ is $Q(c_T)$. These formulas are given by [lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization] (every complex is resolving, as $A,B$ are exact) for some adjunction $d$ between the lift's left derived pair and $\bar b$ (resp. $\bar a$); $d$ is the lift's adjunction $d_0$. Indeed $d$ and $d_0$ have the same functors, so $d$'s Hom bijection is $\psi\circ$ that of $d_0$ for a natural automorphism $\psi$ of the right adjoint. Every object is $QI$ with $I$ K-injective [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Choose a quasi-isomorphism $s:P'\to bI$ from a flat-term K-flat complex $P'$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The isomorphism $y=\eta^b_I\,Q(s)$ has the same inverse transpose under $d_0$ (the lift's canonical formula) and under $d$ (the resolving-class formula), namely the left comparison followed by $Q$ of the ordinary transpose of $s$. Hence $\psi_{QI}y=y$, so $\psi=1$; likewise for $a$. The exact localization comparisons are suppressed throughout, as in the statement.

source.place: Tags 0736 (lemma-base-change-map-flat-case), 07A7 (remark-base-change), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), 0FPI (lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility). Formal normalization calculation by NW.

proof.text:
Let $t:Rb\xrightarrow{\sim}aS$ be the ordinary right-adjoint commutation isomorphism determined by the specified ring-compatible square. Let $\tau:\bar R\bar b\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar a\bar S$ be the conjugate of its canonical derived pullback square. For the two paths from $\mathcal X'$ to $\mathcal Y$, apply the normalized composition comparisons, and insert the specified 2-isomorphism between their composite morphisms. Their right-derived-unit formulas, composed with one another, give for every complex $T$ on $\mathcal X'$:
$$\tau_{QT}\,\bar R(\eta^b_T)\,\eta^R_{bT}
=\bar a(\eta^S_T)\,\eta^a_{ST}\,Q(t_T).\tag{*}$$
Explicitly each path comparison identifies its common-composite resolution transformation with $\bar R(\eta^b_T)\eta^R_{bT}$ or $\bar a(\eta^S_T)\eta^a_{ST}$, after its ordinary path isomorphism. The 2-isomorphism comparison identifies the two common-composite units with the ordinary right path isomorphism inserted. Cancelling the invertible path comparisons gives (*). These theorems assert their unit formulas on every complex, so no injectivity condition on $T$, $bT$ or $ST$ enters.

proof.text:
Rotate the square using the two horizontal adjunctions. The mate-pasting identities applied to the vertical-mate definition of $\beta$ give its horizontal unit-square-counit expression
$$\beta_K=c^D_{\bar S BK}\,A(\tau_{BK})\,A\bar R(u^D_K).\tag{**}$$
Here $\tau$ is precisely the full right conjugate of the same specified pullback square: composition comparisons and the square 2-isomorphism were taken with their canonical adjunction compatibility in step 2. Thus (**) concerns the specified $\beta$, rather than a newly defined comparison. At the ordinary level the identical rotation gives
$$e_P=c_{SBP}\,A(t_{BP})\,AR(u_P).\tag{***}$$
Both rotations are instances of pasting mates along the adjunctions and their unit/counit squares; after expansion, the internal adjacent unit-counit pairs cancel by the triangle identities.

proof.text:
Put $W=BP$ and $X=QP$. Substitute the first normalization from step 1 into (**), then use naturality of $\eta^R$ for the chain map $u_P:P\to bW$. This yields
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_X A(\eta^R_P)
&=c^D_{\bar S QW}\,A\bigl(\tau_{QW}\,\bar R(\eta^b_W)\,\eta^R_{bW}\,Q(Ru_P)\bigr)\\
&=c^D_{\bar S QW}\,A\bigl(\bar a(\eta^S_W)\,\eta^a_{SW}\,Q(t_W)\,Q(Ru_P)\bigr),
\end{aligned}$$
where the second equality is (*) at $T=W$. All products in these formulas mean composition with the rightmost map applied first. Every map is typed in the ordinary unbounded derived category: in particular $\eta^S_W:Q(SW)\to\bar S(QW)$ need not be invertible.

source.place: Tags 0736 (lemma-base-change-map-flat-case), 07A7 (remark-base-change), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), 0FPI (lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility). Formal normalization calculation by NW.

proof.text:
Naturality of the derived horizontal counit for $\eta^S_W$ replaces
$c^D_{\bar S QW}\,A\bar a(\eta^S_W)$ by $\eta^S_W\,c^D_{Q(SW)}$. The second normalization of step 1 at the complex $SW$ then gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_X A(\eta^R_P)
&=\eta^S_W\,Q(c_{SW})\,Q(A(t_W))\,Q(AR(u_P))\\
&=\eta^S_W\,Q\bigl(c_{SW}\,A(t_W)\,AR(u_P)\bigr)
=\eta^S_{BP}\,Q(e_P),
\end{aligned}$$
using (***) in the last equality. With $A=g^*$, $B=(g')^*$, $R=f_*$ and $S=f'_*$, this is the required equality. Only horizontal pullbacks were assumed exact. Neither $\eta^R_P$ nor $\eta^S_{BP}$ was cancelled; hence the calculation applies to arbitrary bounded below $P$ with no acyclicity assumptions.
